newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge refuses to hold Romanov jewels in Texas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge refuses to hold Romanov jewels in Texas.

text.p: A U.S. judge on Friday denied a request from a Texas family seeking to block the Romanov jewelry collection from leaving Houston at the end of a current exhibition here.
The family had hoped to use the jewels to force the Russian government to give them back a St. Petersburg piano factory expropriated after the 1917 Bolshevik revolution.

The priceless collection belonged to the Romanov dynasty that ruled Russia for 300 years. It has been on display at the Houston Museum of Fine Arts since May, but the exhibition was scheduled to close on Sunday and go on to San Diego.

U.S. Judge David Hittner said in a hearing he would not grant a temporary restraining order sought by attorney Lee Magness, also a plaintiff, to keep the jewels here until the piano factory dispute was settled.
Russian Federation attorney Tim Dickenson said an order to keep the jewels here would "cause irreparable damage between the countries."
Magness said he may file another request next week for a preliminary injunction to make sure the jewels do not leave the United States.
Dickenson said the jewels would go to Memphis after San Diego and then on to other cities under an agreement to put them on display in the United States for a year.
In April the collection was held in a van parked on a Washington, D.C., street for several days because of Russian demands for a bigger cut of the exhibition revenues.

Magness said he, his mother and his aunt have been trying since 1994 to get back the Schroder piano factory but the Russian government has refused on grounds that it was a national treasure. He estimated its worth at $650 million.
